elements.element: Vendor defends Customer against covered third-party claims
elements.evidence: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates

elements.element: Coverage: third-party IP infringement allegation as to Services or Deliverables
elements.evidence: (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right

elements.element: Coverage: data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor

elements.element: Coverage: Vendor gross negligence / wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct
shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim

elements.element: Procedure: control of defence by indemnifying party
elements.evidence: the indemnifying Party shall control the defence and settlement
shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: 20.2 ... to the extent arising out of content or materials Customer provides to Vendor or Customer's breach of Applicable Law
(a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right
20.4 ... Customer's unauthorized modification ... combination with items not supplied ... compliance with Customer's written specifications
20.5 ... procure the rights ... modify or replace ... receive a refund of Fees paid

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No super-cap or 3× annual fees language appears anywhere in the redlined clause

offending_extra_words: provided it may not settle in a way that imposes a non-monetary obligation or admission on the indemnified Party without its consent
and may participate with its own counsel at its own cost

20.4 Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables, their combination with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications.

20.5 For a claim under Section 20.1(a), Vendor shall at its expense procure the rights necessary for Customer's continued use, or modify or replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item; if neither is commercially practicable, Customer may terminate the affected Services and receive a refund of Fees paid for the affected item allocable to the unused period.
reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are present and operative: Vendor defence/indemnity for the four coverage heads, Customer affiliates as indemnitees, notice/control/cooperation procedure, and the Customer indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
The fallback level is incomplete because no super-cap of 3× annual fees is imposed on the Vendor indemnity; however, the locked target is preferred, which is satisfied.

Minimality fails: the edit imports fallback-only material (Section 20.4 exclusions and Section 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund remedies) plus settlement-consent and participate-with-own-counsel mechanics beyond the preferred notice/control/cooperation package, expanding 22 words to 279.

Recommend trimming to the preferred scope — drop 20.4 and 20.5 and the settlement proviso/own-counsel language — or anchor the added remedies as a separate, narrowly targeted insertion if Section 9.3's cross-reference truly requires them.
Intent is preserved: no undefined terms, contradictions, or dangling mechanics are introduced, and the replaced one-sided Customer indemnity is properly re-scoped rather than deleted.
